newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - March 3.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - March 3.

text.p: The following stories were reported in Monday's electronic version of The Wall Street Journal:

* CSX and Conrail are close to a pact that would raise the purchase price for Conrail by $1 billion to $10.5 billion, but Norfolk Southern would buy almost half of Conrail's Northeastern routes after the deal closes.

* The Federal Communications Commission is expected to set plans for two airwave auctions, including one for a wireless technology that could intensify competition in the local-telephone and cable-television businesses.
* CIGNA's agreement to acquire HealthSource will enhance Cigna's managed-care business, but the deal could also pose risks because of growing pains at HealthSource.
* Staples agreed to give the Federal Trade Commission another week to review Staple's planned acquisition of Office Depot for possible antitrust issues.
* The Gross Domestic Product expanded at a 3.9 percent annual rate in the fourth quarter.
* The New York Yankees were close to completing a 10-year marketing pact with Adidas, but people familiar with the matter say Fila has reentered the picture.
* Motorola is expected to announce a plan to license and sell software from VocalTec allowing coporations to make phone calls via Internet.
* McDonald's said franchises agreed on a plan to improve sales by offering 55-cent sandwiches.
* Andersen Consulting is expected to report 1996 revenues of more than $5 billion as it and other consulting companies brought in record revenues.
* Disk-drive industry veterans plan to unveil technology that they say can result in computer storage devices with 10 times the capacity of current ones.
* Japan appears prepared to drop its analog high-definition television system.
* Nextel plans a new pricing strategy based on seconds of usage, which could pressure rivals to cut rates.
* Ford Motor is likely to be disappointed if it expects its planned public offering of Hertz shares to provide a quick boost for Ford's own lackluster market valuation. -- Heard on the Street.
* Mention the consumer price index these days and what usually springs to mind, Pavlovian-style, is how it overstates inflation.

Stephen Roach must not have been properly conditioned. Not only does the chief economist of Morgan Stanley Group deny that the CPI overstates inflation, he says it understates the rate at which prices are rising by as much as one-half percentage point. -- Credit Markets.
